newsitem.title: USA: GM says Canada strike idles 100 more in US.
newsitem.headline: GM says Canada strike idles 100 more in US.

text.p: General Motors Corp said that as of 11 a.m. EDT Thursday, it was forced to idle an additional 100 U.S. workers because of the Canadian Auto Workers' strike.

GM said it sent another 100 workers home at its Ypsilanti, Mich. transmission plant, bringing the total number of workers idled at that facility to 900. GM has a total of 1,950 U.S. workers idled by the Canadian strike, including 1,050 workers at its North Tonawanda, N.Y., engine plant near Buffalo.

All 26,000 CAW-GM workers are now on strike, but GM executives said Wednesday that the company's U.S. plants are not in immediate danger of running out of critical parts from Canada. The escalating walkout began October 3.
